_readme: OPTIONAL per-env override for the contract_br provisioning depth.
By default SMF needs nothing here: contract_br creates exactly the same BR setup as
'Assign apiKey to BR' — same two rules (3 Static, 4 Dynamic), same parent conditions
(STATIC/DYNAMIC_MARKUP_PARENT_CONDITION_ID), same outputDetailIds and markup values
(10% and 15%-25%), same overwrite/executionOrder. The ONLY difference is what the
condition matches on: inputDetailId 30 ('contractId IN') with the contract id list as
inputValue, instead of inputDetailId 26 with the apiKey. See
CrawlaBusinessRulesProvisioner.provision_for_contracts.
The apiKey path also does a rule-CONFIG assignment (POST /v1/apikeys/create-assign/
rule/{id}). That endpoint is apiKey-only, so it has no contract counterpart and is
skipped — the conditions are what differ per input.
Fill an env in ONLY to override that default, e.g. if its ids differ. Keys:
contract_value_field : which contract attribute becomes inputValue. Default
'autoId' — the short numeric id (e.g. 10103) that
'contractId IN' matches; SMF reads it back from Backoffice
after creating each contract. 'uid' and 'id' (mongo _id)
are also available.
value_mode           : 'join' (default) puts every contract in ONE condition as a
separated list, which is what operator IN expects.
'per_contract' creates one condition per contract instead.
value_separator      : default ','.
conditions           : raw rule-value-mapping bodies, POSTed verbatim except for
inputValue. Setting this REPLACES the mirrored default.
Supports 'children' (nested conditions, each created with
parentRuleValueMappingId set to its parent's LIVE id) and
'inject_input_value': false for an operator-only test.
Note: a rule's root conditions already exist in BR and are referenced by id, never
created — trying to create one returns 400 AlreadyExistsException. SMF parses that
error, reuses the existing id, and never deletes it on teardown.
Teardown deletes only what SMF created, in reverse creation order (BR refuses to
delete a parent while a child still points at it).
